title: Drug Target and Biomarker Discovery Laboratory
text:
Research Areas


Activity-Based Probes
We develop activity-based probes to monitor enzyme function in cells, animals, and disease models, with particular interest in proteases relevant to neurodegenerative diseases.


Molecular Biomarker Discovery and Fluorescent Probe Development
We design chemical tools and fluorescent probes to detect disease-associated molecular activities and support biomarker discovery.


Peptidomimetic Transporters
We develop peptoid and peptidomimetic scaffolds for organelle targeting and intracellular delivery of biologically active cargos.

title: Drug Target and Biomarker Discovery Laboratory
text: We welcome motivated students and researchers interested in chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, molecular probes, drug target discovery, biomarker identification, and disease-relevant small-molecule tools.

Research Interests
Prospective students and collaborators are encouraged to contact us if they are interested in one or more of the following areas:

Drug target discovery and target validation
Biomarker discovery and fluorescence-based detection
Chemical biology and molecular probe development
Protease biology and activity-based probes
Peptidomimetic transporters and intracellular delivery
AI-assisted peptide and protein binder design

title: Research
text:
Our lab develops and applies small-molecule chemical tools to identify drug targets, study enzyme activity, and discover biomarkers relevant to neurodegenerative diseases and cancer.


  
    
    
      1. Activity-Based Probes to Monitor Enzyme Activity
      Activity-based probes react with specific classes of enzymes in a manner that correlates with enzyme activity, enabling monitoring of enzyme function and activity in cells, animals, and disease models. Our lab develops probes for various proteases to study the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
    
  

  
    
    
      2. Molecular Biomarker Discovery and Fluorescent Probe Development
      We design chemical tools and fluorescent probes to detect disease-associated molecular activities and support biomarker discovery. Our probes enable imaging of enzyme activity in living cells and tissues.
    
  

  
    
    
      3. Organelle-Targeting Peptidomimetics as Molecular Transporters
      Peptoids have unique advantages over other polymeric delivery scaffolds because they share physiological and chemical properties with peptides and proteins while offering superior metabolic and immunological stability. We develop mitochondria- and cell-targeting peptoids for intracellular delivery of small-molecule, protein, and nanoparticle cargos.
